example_sentences.japanese: 週末に祖母と公園へ行きます。
example_sentences.english: On the weekend I go to the park with my grandmother.
example_sentences.furigana: 週[しゅう]末[まつ]に祖[そ]母[ぼ]と公[こう]園[えん]へ行[い]きます。

example_sentences.japanese: 昨日、祖母に会いました。
example_sentences.furigana: 昨日[きのう]、祖[そ]母[ぼ]に会[あ]いました。

items.reading_composition: Kana only — the word is written exactly as it is read.
items.meaning_mnemonic: An old woman dozes in a sunbeam and lets out a long, satisfied <reading>おばあさん</reading> — <reading>"ohh, baa, sun"</reading> — and that sigh is exactly what you call your <vocabulary>grandmother (polite)</vocabulary>.
items.description: Also used to politely address any elderly woman, not just your own grandmother.

example_sentences.japanese: 私のおばあさんはお茶を飲みます。
example_sentences.furigana: 私[わたし]のおばあさんはお茶[ちゃ]を飲[の]みます。

example_sentences.japanese: 週末、おばあさんと映画を見ます。
example_sentences.english: On the weekend, I watch a movie with my grandmother.
example_sentences.furigana: 週[しゅう]末[まつ]、おばあさんと映[えい]画[が]を見[み]ます。

example_sentences.japanese: おばあさんは明日家に来ます。
example_sentences.english: Grandmother is coming to our house tomorrow.
example_sentences.furigana: おばあさんは明日[あした]家[いえ]に来[き]ます。

items.reading_composition: Irregular — おじ cannot be assembled from the dictionary readings of 叔父.
items.meaning_mnemonic: A backup <kanji>father</kanji> who shows up every holiday, spoils you rotten, and sneaks you extra sweets is your <vocabulary>uncle</vocabulary>.
items.reading_mnemonic: Every holiday the backup dad sneaks you so many extra sweets that your parents gasp '<reading>oh, gee</reading>', the <reading>おじ</reading> sound that follows your spoiling <vocabulary form="叔父">uncle</vocabulary> everywhere.
items.description: An uncle younger than your parent; an older one uses different kanji, same reading.

example_sentences.japanese: 叔父と公園で遊んだ。
example_sentences.english: I played with my uncle at the park.
example_sentences.furigana: 叔父[おじ]と公[こう]園[えん]で遊[あそ]んだ。

example_sentences.japanese: 週末、叔父の家に行く。
example_sentences.english: On the weekend, I go to my uncle's house.
example_sentences.furigana: 週[しゅう]末[まつ]、叔父[おじ]の家[いえ]に行[い]く。

example_sentences.japanese: 叔父は毎日お茶を飲む。
example_sentences.english: My uncle drinks tea every day.
example_sentences.furigana: 叔父[おじ]は毎[まい]日[にち]お茶[ちゃ]を飲[の]む。

items.reading_composition: Irregular — おば cannot be assembled from the dictionary readings of 叔母.
items.meaning_mnemonic: A <kanji>mother</kanji> figure who's still just a <kanji>youth</kanji> herself, holding kids anyway, is your <vocabulary>aunt</vocabulary>.
items.reading_mnemonic: Still a youth herself, your <vocabulary form="叔母">aunt</vocabulary> holds the little cousins on her lap anyway and calms them with one squeaky <reading>oboe</reading> note that sounds just like <reading>おば</reading>.
items.description: An aunt younger than your parent; an older one uses different kanji, same reading.

example_sentences.japanese: 私の叔母は毎朝コーヒーを飲みます。
example_sentences.english: My aunt drinks coffee every morning.
example_sentences.furigana: 私[わたし]の叔母[おば]は毎[まい]朝[あさ]コーヒーを飲[の]みます。

example_sentences.japanese: 明日叔母と一緒に海に行きます。
example_sentences.english: Tomorrow I'm going to the sea with my aunt.
example_sentences.furigana: 明日[あした]叔母[おば]と一[いっ]緒[しょ]に海[うみ]に行[い]きます。

example_sentences.japanese: 先週叔母の家でご飯を食べました。
example_sentences.english: Last week I ate a meal at my aunt's house.
example_sentences.furigana: 先[せん]週[しゅう]叔母[おば]の家[いえ]でご飯[はん]を食[た]べました。

items.meaning_mnemonic: The <kanji>child</kanji> you proudly <kanji>offer</kanji> up to the neighbors, freshly bathed and squirming, is simply your <vocabulary>child</vocabulary>.
items.description: Sometimes written partly in hiragana, since the second kanji once meant "servant."

example_sentences.japanese: 子供が公園で遊ぶ。
example_sentences.english: A child plays in the park.
example_sentences.furigana: 子[こ]供[ども]が公[こう]園[えん]で遊[あそ]ぶ。

example_sentences.japanese: 私の子供は本を読む。
example_sentences.furigana: 私[わたし]の子[こ]供[ども]は本[ほん]を読[よ]む。

example_sentences.japanese: 子供と一緒に映画を見る。
example_sentences.english: I watch a movie with my child.
example_sentences.furigana: 子[こ]供[ども]と一[いっ]緒[しょ]に映[えい]画[が]を見[み]る。

items.reading_composition: Irregular — むすこ cannot be assembled from the dictionary readings of 息子.
items.meaning_mnemonic: This household's only <kanji>child</kanji> happens to be a boy, so the family just calls him their <vocabulary>son</vocabulary>.
items.reading_mnemonic: The household's only child is a boy in a <reading>Moose Co.</reading> cap, so when the family calls 「<reading>むすこ</reading>」 at dinner, everyone knows they mean their <vocabulary form="息子">son</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 私の息子は学生です。
example_sentences.furigana: 私[わたし]の息子[むすこ]は学[がく]生[せい]です。

example_sentences.japanese: 息子は毎日学校に行きます。
example_sentences.english: My son goes to school every day.
example_sentences.furigana: 息子[むすこ]は毎[まい]日[にち]学[がっ]校[こう]に行[い]きます。

example_sentences.japanese: 父と息子は映画を見ます。
example_sentences.english: Father and son watch a movie.
example_sentences.furigana: 父[ちち]と息子[むすこ]は映[えい]画[が]を見[み]ます。

items.meaning_mnemonic: Every family has one child who gets away with everything, and in this house that's always the <vocabulary>daughter</vocabulary>.
items.reading_mnemonic: In this house the one child who gets away with everything is <reading>Moose May</reading>, dragging her toy moose across the clean floor while her parents only sigh 「<reading>むすめ</reading>」 at their <vocabulary form="娘">daughter</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 私の娘は学校に行きます。
example_sentences.furigana: 私[わたし]の娘[むすめ]は学[がっ]校[こう]に行[い]きます。

example_sentences.japanese: 娘と一緒に映画を見ました。
example_sentences.english: I watched a movie with my daughter.
example_sentences.furigana: 娘[むすめ]と一[いっ]緒[しょ]に映[えい]画[が]を見[み]ました。

example_sentences.japanese: 娘は朝ご飯を食べます。
example_sentences.furigana: 娘[むすめ]は朝[あさ]ご飯[はん]を食[た]べます。

items.word_type: な adjective, noun, の adjective
items.reading_composition: Irregular — おとな cannot be assembled from the dictionary readings of 大人.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Once a <kanji>person</kanji> gets <kanji>big</kanji> enough, everyone starts calling them an <vocabulary>adult</vocabulary>.
items.reading_mnemonic: Once little <reading>Otto Nana</reading> grows big enough to bump his head on the doorframe, the whole family starts calling him 「<reading>おとな</reading>」, a full-grown <vocabulary form="大人">adult</vocabulary>.
items.description: As a な adjective, it takes な directly before the noun it describes, not い like most descriptive words.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女は大人です。
example_sentences.furigana: 彼[かの]女[じょ]は大人[おとな]です。

example_sentences.japanese: 大人はお酒を飲みます。
example_sentences.furigana: 大人[おとな]はお酒[さけ]を飲[の]みます。

example_sentences.japanese: 大人と子供が公園に行きます。
example_sentences.english: Adults and children go to the park.
example_sentences.furigana: 大人[おとな]と子[こ]供[ども]が公[こう]園[えん]に行[い]きます。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 兄（きょう）＋弟（だい）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.meaning_mnemonic: An <kanji>older brother</kanji> and a <kanji>younger brother</kanji> together are what everyone calls <vocabulary>siblings</vocabulary>.
items.description: Covers siblings in general, including sisters, even though both kanji individually mean brother.

example_sentences.japanese: 私の兄弟は学生です。
example_sentences.furigana: 私[わたし]の兄[きょう]弟[だい]は学[がく]生[せい]です。

example_sentences.japanese: 兄弟と一緒に映画を見る。
example_sentences.english: I watch a movie with my siblings.
example_sentences.furigana: 兄[きょう]弟[だい]と一[いっ]緒[しょ]に映[えい]画[が]を見[み]る。

example_sentences.japanese: 週末に兄弟と遊ぶ。
example_sentences.english: I hang out with my siblings on the weekend.
example_sentences.furigana: 週[しゅう]末[まつ]に兄[きょう]弟[だい]と遊[あそ]ぶ。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — ご＋主（しゅ）＋人（じん）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: The master of the house: goshujin.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The <kanji>main</kanji> <kanji>person</kanji> running a household is what you call someone's <vocabulary>husband</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: ご主人は今日、忙しいですか。
example_sentences.furigana: ご主[しゅ]人[じん]は今日[きょう]、忙[いそが]しいですか。

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女のご主人に会いました。
example_sentences.furigana: 彼[かの]女[じょ]のご主[しゅ]人[じん]に会[あ]いました。

example_sentences.japanese: ご主人と一緒にご飯を食べます。
example_sentences.english: We're having a meal with your husband.
example_sentences.furigana: ご主[しゅ]人[じん]と一[いっ]緒[しょ]にご飯[はん]を食[た]べます。

items.mnemonic_text: The one in the back rooms: okusan.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Whoever rules the <kanji>interior</kanji> of the house earns the title <vocabulary>wife</vocabulary>.
items.reading_mnemonic: From an <reading>oak</reading> chair deep in the house's interior she rules every room, so visitors bow and greet her 「<reading>おくさん</reading>」, the <vocabulary form="奥さん">wife</vocabulary> of the house.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼の奥さんに会いました。
example_sentences.furigana: 彼[かれ]の奥[おく]さんに会[あ]いました。

example_sentences.japanese: 奥さんは晩ご飯を食べます。
example_sentences.furigana: 奥[おく]さんは晩[ばん]ご飯[はん]を食[た]べます。

example_sentences.japanese: 友達の奥さんが来ました。
example_sentences.furigana: 友[とも]達[だち]の奥[おく]さんが来[き]ました。

items.meaning_mnemonic: The person who knows exactly where every spare key in the house is hidden is your <vocabulary>wife</vocabulary>.
items.reading_mnemonic: You lose the house key again, and only your <vocabulary form="妻">wife</vocabulary> knows where the spares hide. Digging one out, she sighs a weary <reading>too-mah</reading>, the <reading>つま</reading> sound of every lost-key morning.

example_sentences.japanese: 私の妻は今忙しいです。
example_sentences.english: My wife is busy right now.
example_sentences.furigana: 私[わたし]の妻[つま]は今[いま]忙[いそが]しいです。

example_sentences.japanese: 妻と一緒に映画を見ます。
example_sentences.english: I watch a movie with my wife.
example_sentences.furigana: 妻[つま]と一[いっ]緒[しょ]に映[えい]画[が]を見[み]ます。

example_sentences.japanese: 週末は妻と公園に行きます。
example_sentences.english: On the weekend I go to the park with my wife.
example_sentences.furigana: 週[しゅう]末[まつ]は妻[つま]と公[こう]園[えん]に行[い]きます。

items.meaning_mnemonic: The one who groans the loudest fixing a leaky faucet at 2 AM is your <vocabulary>husband</vocabulary>.
items.reading_mnemonic: At 2 AM the leaky faucet sprays him in the face, and between groans your <vocabulary form="夫">husband</vocabulary> yelps <reading>おっと</reading>, a startled '<reading>oh, toe</reading>' as the wrench lands on his foot.

example_sentences.japanese: 私の夫は毎日忙しいです。
example_sentences.english: My husband is busy every day.
example_sentences.furigana: 私[わたし]の夫[おっと]は毎[まい]日[にち]忙[いそが]しいです。

example_sentences.japanese: 夫と一緒に映画を見ます。
example_sentences.english: I watch movies with my husband.
example_sentences.furigana: 夫[おっと]と一[いっ]緒[しょ]に映[えい]画[が]を見[み]ます。

example_sentences.japanese: 夫はコーヒーを飲みます。
example_sentences.furigana: 夫[おっと]はコーヒーを飲[の]みます。

items.meaning_mnemonic: The <kanji>person</kanji> kanji and the <vocabulary>person</vocabulary> word are exactly the same, so they mean the same thing.
items.reading_mnemonic: One leg stays planted while the other steps out on tiptoe, so you whisper '<reading>he toes</reading>' as the lone walker passes: a single <reading>ひと</reading>, one <vocabulary form="人">person</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: あの人は先生です。
example_sentences.furigana: あの人[ひと]は先[せん]生[せい]です。

example_sentences.japanese: 私は毎日あの人と話します。
example_sentences.english: I talk with that person every day.
example_sentences.furigana: 私[わたし]は毎[まい]日[にち]あの人[ひと]と話[はな]します。

example_sentences.japanese: 公園でいい人に会います。
example_sentences.english: I meet a nice person at the park.
example_sentences.furigana: 公[こう]園[えん]でいい人[ひと]に会[あ]います。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 友（とも）＋達（だち）. Rendaku: 達 たち → だち.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Two hands closing together as a <kanji>friend</kanji> finally <kanji>reach</kanji> each other, and that arrival is what makes a <vocabulary>friend</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 私は友達と映画を見ます。
example_sentences.english: I watch a movie with my friend.
example_sentences.furigana: 私[わたし]は友[とも]達[だち]と映[えい]画[が]を見[み]ます。

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女はいい友達です。
example_sentences.furigana: 彼[かの]女[じょ]はいい友[とも]達[だち]です。

example_sentences.japanese: 週末に友達と遊びます。
example_sentences.english: I hang out with friends on the weekend.
example_sentences.furigana: 週[しゅう]末[まつ]に友[とも]達[だち]と遊[あそ]びます。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 先（せん）＋生（せい）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: The one born before you in knowledge: sensei.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Someone whose <kanji>life</kanji> is already <kanji>ahead</kanji> of yours on the path knows the way, which makes them your <vocabulary>teacher</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 先生は学校に行きます。
example_sentences.furigana: 先[せん]生[せい]は学[がっ]校[こう]に行[い]きます。

example_sentences.japanese: 私は先生に聞きました。
example_sentences.furigana: 私[わたし]は先[せん]生[せい]に聞[き]きました。

example_sentences.japanese: あの先生はいい人です。
example_sentences.english: That teacher is a good person.
example_sentences.furigana: あの先[せん]生[せい]はいい人[ひと]です。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 学（がく）＋生（せい）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: One in the life of study: gakusei.
items.meaning_mnemonic: A <kanji>life</kanji> spent buried in books, with nothing to show for it yet but <kanji>study</kanji>, is exactly what we call a <vocabulary>student</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 私は学生です。
example_sentences.furigana: 私[わたし]は学[がく]生[せい]です。

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は学生ですか。
example_sentences.furigana: 彼[かれ]は学[がく]生[せい]ですか。

example_sentences.japanese: 学生は本を読みます。
example_sentences.furigana: 学[がく]生[せい]は本[ほん]を読[よ]みます。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 生（せい）＋徒（と）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.meaning_mnemonic: A <kanji>life</kanji> still in its <kanji>junior</kanji> stage, trailing a few steps behind the teacher, is a <vocabulary>pupil</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 私の弟は生徒です。
example_sentences.english: My younger brother is a pupil.
example_sentences.furigana: 私[わたし]の弟[おとうと]は生[せい]徒[と]です。

example_sentences.japanese: 先生は生徒と話します。
example_sentences.english: The teacher talks with the pupils.
example_sentences.furigana: 先[せん]生[せい]は生[せい]徒[と]と話[はな]します。

example_sentences.japanese: 生徒は毎朝学校に行きます。
example_sentences.english: The pupils go to school every morning.
example_sentences.furigana: 生[せい]徒[と]は毎[まい]朝[あさ]学[がっ]校[こう]に行[い]きます。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 医（い）＋者（しゃ）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Whoever pulls the arrow out and shuts it away already practices <kanji>medicine</kanji>. Add the <kanji>person</kanji> doing it and you have a <vocabulary>doctor</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 明日、医者に行きます。
example_sentences.english: I'm going to the doctor tomorrow.
example_sentences.furigana: 明日[あした]、医[い]者[しゃ]に行[い]きます。

example_sentences.japanese: 医者は今、忙しいです。
example_sentences.english: The doctor is busy right now.
example_sentences.furigana: 医[い]者[しゃ]は今[いま]、忙[いそが]しいです。

example_sentences.japanese: 友達と一緒に医者を待ちます。
example_sentences.english: I'll wait for the doctor with my friend.
example_sentences.furigana: 友[とも]達[だち]と一[いっ]緒[しょ]に医[い]者[しゃ]を待[ま]ちます。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 会（かい）＋社（しゃ）＋員（いん）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Everyone who <kanji>meets</kanji> here for a paycheck is an <kanji>employee</kanji>, one more mouth this place must feed. That makes them a <vocabulary>company employee</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 会社員の友達とお茶を飲みます。
example_sentences.english: I drink tea with my friend who's a company employee.
example_sentences.furigana: 会[かい]社[しゃ]員[いん]の友[とも]達[だち]とお茶[ちゃ]を飲[の]みます。

example_sentences.japanese: 明日、会社員の兄に会います。
example_sentences.english: Tomorrow I'm meeting my older brother, who's a company employee.
example_sentences.furigana: 明日[あした]、会[かい]社[しゃ]員[いん]の兄[あに]に会[あ]います。

example_sentences.japanese: 母は会社員ではありません。
example_sentences.english: My mother is not a company employee.
example_sentences.furigana: 母[はは]は会[かい]社[しゃ]員[いん]ではありません。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 駅（えき）＋員（いん）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Someone has to run the <kanji>station</kanji> where tired horses get swapped for fresh ones. That <kanji>employee</kanji>, one more mouth the station feeds, is the <vocabulary>station staff</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 駅員に聞きます。
example_sentences.furigana: 駅[えき]員[いん]に聞[き]きます。

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女は駅員です。
example_sentences.furigana: 彼[かの]女[じょ]は駅[えき]員[いん]です。

example_sentences.japanese: 今日駅員に会いました。
example_sentences.english: I met the station staff today.
example_sentences.furigana: 今日[きょう]駅[えき]員[いん]に会[あ]いました。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 警（けい）＋官（かん）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.meaning_mnemonic: A <kanji>government</kanji> official whose whole job is to <kanji>admonish</kanji> you is a <vocabulary>police officer</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 公園で警官を見ました。
example_sentences.english: I saw a police officer at the park.
example_sentences.furigana: 公[こう]園[えん]で警[けい]官[かん]を見[み]ました。

example_sentences.japanese: 警官が家に来ました。
example_sentences.english: A police officer came to the house.
example_sentences.furigana: 警[けい]官[かん]が家[いえ]に来[き]ました。

example_sentences.japanese: 昨日、警官に会いました。
example_sentences.english: Yesterday I met a police officer.
example_sentences.furigana: 昨日[きのう]、警[けい]官[かん]に会[あ]いました。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 外（がい）＋国（こく）＋人（じん）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Step <kanji>outside</kanji> the walled <kanji>country</kanji> that guards its one jewel, and any <kanji>person</kanji> you meet there is a <vocabulary>foreigner</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は外国人です。
example_sentences.furigana: 彼[かれ]は外[がい]国[こく]人[じん]です。

example_sentences.japanese: 外国人とお茶を飲みました。

items.meaning_mnemonic: Sit down to a <kanji>meal</kanji> while the <kanji>morning</kanji> moon still hangs in the window, and that meal is <vocabulary>breakfast</vocabulary>.

items.reading_composition: Mixed — 昼（ひる）kun'yomi ＋ ご ＋ 飯（はん）on'yomi.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The sun climbs until it hits <kanji>noon</kanji> and the whole working day halts for one <kanji>meal</kanji>. That break in the middle is <vocabulary>lunch</vocabulary>.

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 晩（ばん）＋ご＋飯（はん）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Nobody is allowed near the <kanji>meal</kanji> until <kanji>nightfall</kanji>, and the spread they finally fall on is <vocabulary>dinner</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.english: I eat dinner with my family.
example_sentences.furigana: 私[わたし]は家[か]族[ぞく]と晩[ばん]ご飯[はん]を食[た]べます。

example_sentences.japanese: 晩ご飯は何時ですか。
example_sentences.furigana: 晩[ばん]ご飯[はん]は何[なん]時[じ]ですか。

items.reading_composition: Kana only — the word is written exactly as it is read.
items.meaning_mnemonic: A baker too cheap to buy an oven fries every loaf of <vocabulary>bread</vocabulary> in one battered <reading>pan</reading>. Ask him what it is and he just grunts <reading>パン</reading>.

example_sentences.furigana: このパンはおいしいです。

example_sentences.japanese: パンはいくらですか。
example_sentences.furigana: パンはいくらですか。

items.meaning_mnemonic: Overnight, every shelf in Koichi's konbini is restocked with nothing but <vocabulary>meat</vocabulary>. Cold steaks fill the onigiri rack, sausages crowd the drinks fridge, and a slab of ribs beeps through the till.

items.mnemonic_text: The swimmer on your plate: sakana.

items.reading_mnemonic: Ana wades into the flooded rice field and scoops the crouching <vocabulary form="魚">fish</vocabulary> up in her wet <reading>sock</reading>, so <reading>sock-Ana</reading>'s catch, 「<reading>さかな</reading>」, goes straight into the pan over the fire.

example_sentences.japanese: 母は魚を買いました。
example_sentences.furigana: 母[はは]は魚[さかな]を買[か]いました。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 野（や）＋菜（さい）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Green things that come up on their own out on the untended <kanji>plains</kanji>, with no farmer and no fence, still get gathered up and eaten as <vocabulary>vegetables</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 朝ごはんに野菜を食べます。
example_sentences.furigana: 朝[あさ]ごはんに野[や]菜[さい]を食[た]べます。

example_sentences.japanese: この野菜は安いです。

example_sentences.furigana: 母[はは]と一[いっ]緒[しょ]に野[や]菜[さい]を買[か]います。

items.reading_composition: Irregular — くだもの cannot be assembled from the dictionary readings of 果物.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Out of everything hanging in a tree, the one <kanji>thing</kanji> sweet enough to be worth climbing for is <vocabulary>fruit</vocabulary>.
items.reading_mnemonic: The farmer yells <reading>Cooda Moe, no!</reading> as his monkey climbs to the top of the tree for the one sweet <vocabulary form="果物">fruit</vocabulary> worth the climb, and 「<reading>くだもの</reading>」 echoes through the orchard.

example_sentences.japanese: 私は毎朝果物を食べます。
example_sentences.furigana: 私[わたし]は毎[まい]朝[あさ]果物[くだもの]を食[た]べます。

example_sentences.japanese: この果物はおいしいです。
example_sentences.furigana: この果物[くだもの]はおいしいです。

example_sentences.japanese: 母は果物を買いました。
example_sentences.furigana: 母[はは]は果物[くだもの]を買[か]いました。

items.meaning_mnemonic: The smooth white thing in the carton that cracks if you look at it wrong and turns into breakfast the moment it hits a hot pan is an <vocabulary>egg</vocabulary>.
items.reading_mnemonic: The cook cracks a smooth white <vocabulary form="卵">egg</vocabulary> from the carton into the hot pan and yells 「<reading>たまご</reading>」, <reading>tomato, go</reading>, as the red slices slide in beside it.

example_sentences.japanese: 朝ごはんに卵を食べます。
example_sentences.furigana: 朝[あさ]ごはんに卵[たまご]を食[た]べます。

example_sentences.japanese: この卵はおいしいです。
example_sentences.furigana: この卵[たまご]はおいしいです。

example_sentences.japanese: 母は卵を三つ買いました。
example_sentences.furigana: 母[はは]は卵[たまご]を三[みっ]つ買[か]いました。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 牛（ぎゅう）＋乳（にゅう）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.meaning_mnemonic: A <kanji>cow</kanji> makes far more of the white stuff than her one calf could ever drink, so the rest gets bottled and sold as <vocabulary>milk</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 朝ご飯に牛乳を飲みます。
example_sentences.furigana: 朝[あさ]ご飯[はん]に牛[ぎゅう]乳[にゅう]を飲[の]みます。

example_sentences.japanese: この牛乳はおいしいです。
example_sentences.furigana: この牛[ぎゅう]乳[にゅう]はおいしいです。

example_sentences.japanese: 母は牛乳を買いました。
example_sentences.furigana: 母[はは]は牛[ぎゅう]乳[にゅう]を買[か]いました。

items.meaning_mnemonic: The <kanji>water</kanji> kanji and the <vocabulary>water</vocabulary> word are the same, so they carry the same meaning.
items.reading_mnemonic: <reading>Miss Sue</reading> stands under the falling stream as its two trickles splash out to each side, and she calls that cold <vocabulary form="水">water</vocabulary> 「<reading>みず</reading>」.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女は水を買いました。
example_sentences.furigana: 彼[かの]女[じょ]は水[みず]を買[か]いました。

items.meaning_mnemonic: The <kanji>tea</kanji> kanji and the <vocabulary>tea</vocabulary> word mean exactly the same thing; meeting it again as a word changes nothing.
items.description: In everyday Japanese お茶 usually means green tea, not tea in general.

example_sentences.japanese: 毎朝お茶を飲みます。
example_sentences.furigana: 毎[まい]朝[あさ]お茶[ちゃ]を飲[の]みます。

items.reading_composition: Kana only — the word is written exactly as it is read.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Punch the top button on the mountain-trail vending machine and it drops a scalding can with a hiss that sounds like <reading>koh-hee</reading>. That hiss is <reading>コーヒー</reading>, and the can is bitter black <vocabulary>coffee</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 毎朝コーヒーを飲みます。

example_sentences.japanese: コーヒーはいくらですか。
example_sentences.furigana: コーヒーはいくらですか。

items.meaning_mnemonic: Leave cooked rice and clean river water together in a warm, dark cupboard for a few weeks. The mixture quietly ferments into <vocabulary>alcohol / sake</vocabulary>.
items.reading_mnemonic: Old <reading>O'Sakey</reading> opens the warm dark cupboard after three weeks, sniffs the fermented rice and river water inside, and raises a cup to 「<reading>おさけ</reading>」, his <vocabulary form="お酒">sake</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 友達とお酒を飲みます。

example_sentences.japanese: お酒を買いました。

example_sentences.japanese: このお酒はおいしいです。
example_sentences.furigana: このお酒[さけ]はおいしいです。

items.reading_composition: Kana only — the word is written exactly as it is read.
items.meaning_mnemonic: A swarm of bees has taken over the beach bar, and their one <reading>bee rule</reading> is that the taps pour for them first. They only ever order <reading>ビール</reading>, so the whole place reeks of spilled <vocabulary>beer</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 私はビールを飲みます。

example_sentences.japanese: このビールはおいしいです。
example_sentences.furigana: このビールはおいしいです。

example_sentences.japanese: 友達とビールを買いました。
example_sentences.english: I bought beer with a friend.
example_sentences.furigana: 友[とも]達[だち]とビールを買[か]いました。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 砂（さ）＋糖（とう）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Tip the bag and it hisses out like dry <kanji>sand</kanji>. A spoonful of that pale grit turns your coffee sweet, so it has to be <vocabulary>sugar</vocabulary>.

items.meaning_mnemonic: One shake of the white grit makes hot chips worth eating. The same pinch stings like fire in a small cut, because it is <vocabulary>salt</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 母は毎日塩を使います。

example_sentences.furigana: 母[はは]は毎[まい]日[にち]塩[しお]を使[つか]います。

example_sentences.furigana: 友[とも]達[だち]の料[りょう]理[り]を食[た]べました。

items.meaning_mnemonic: On its own, <kanji>food</kanji> is just stuff on a shelf. Make a whole <kanji>matter</kanji> of it, with plates, chopsticks and a set table, and it becomes a <vocabulary>meal</vocabulary>.

items.meaning_mnemonic: The hard little grains straight from the sack, before a drop of water or any heat reaches them, are <vocabulary>uncooked rice</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.furigana: この米[こめ]は安[やす]いです。

example_sentences.japanese: 料理に米を使います。
example_sentences.furigana: 料[りょう]理[り]に米[こめ]を使[つか]います。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — お＋菓（か）＋子（し）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.meaning_mnemonic: <kanji>Cakes</kanji> come in adult size, but shrink each one to <kanji>child</kanji> size and you can eat twelve without comment. A bowl of those miniatures is <vocabulary>sweets / snacks</vocabulary>.

items.meaning_mnemonic: Picture a lunch box split into <kanji>petal</kanji>-shaped compartments, each one holding exactly the <kanji>right</kanji> amount for a single meal. That neatly portioned box is a <vocabulary>boxed lunch</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.furigana: 彼[かの]女[じょ]と弁[べん]当[とう]を食[た]べます。

items.reading_composition: Kana only — the word is written exactly as it is read.

example_sentences.furigana: 友[とも]達[だち]とレストランで食[た]べます。

items.meaning_mnemonic: Fill the <kanji>school</kanji> grounds where the tree-lined paths cross with children who have nothing to do but <kanji>study</kanji>, and that place is a <vocabulary>school</vocabulary>.

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 大（だい）＋学（がく）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.meaning_mnemonic: <kanji>Study</kanji> at a place so <kanji>big</kanji> it has its own bus route, its own bookshops, and its own postcode, and you are standing in a <vocabulary>university</vocabulary>.

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 会（かい）＋社（しゃ）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: The meeting shrine of work: kaisha.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The building you travel to each morning to <kanji>meet</kanji> the same coworkers and do the same job is your <vocabulary>company / office</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.furigana: 私[わたし]は毎[まい]朝[あさ]会[かい]社[しゃ]に行[い]きます。

example_sentences.japanese: 明日友達と会社で会います。
example_sentences.english: Tomorrow I'm meeting a friend at the office.
example_sentences.furigana: 明日[あした]友[とも]達[だち]と会[かい]社[しゃ]で会[あ]います。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 病（びょう）＋院（いん）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.meaning_mnemonic: An <kanji>ill</kanji> body checks into the one <kanji>institution</kanji> built to house the sick until they mend, and that building is a <vocabulary>hospital</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 明日、父と病院に行きます。
example_sentences.english: Tomorrow I'm going to the hospital with my father.
example_sentences.furigana: 明日[あした]、父[ちち]と病[びょう]院[いん]に行[い]きます。

example_sentences.japanese: この病院はあそこです。
example_sentences.furigana: この病[びょう]院[いん]はあそこです。

example_sentences.furigana: 友[とも]達[だち]は病[びょう]院[いん]で本[ほん]を読[よ]みます。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 銀（ぎん）＋行（こう）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.meaning_mnemonic: When you run low on <kanji>silver</kanji>, you <kanji>go</kanji> to one particular crossroads in town. That corner building is the <vocabulary>bank</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 私は銀行に行きます。
example_sentences.furigana: 私[わたし]は銀[ぎん]行[こう]に行[い]きます。

example_sentences.furigana: 銀[ぎん]行[こう]はどこですか。

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は明日銀行で待ちます。

example_sentences.furigana: 彼[かれ]は明日[あした]銀[ぎん]行[こう]で待[ま]ちます。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 郵（ゆう）＋便（びん）＋局（きょく）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.furigana: 郵[ゆう]便[びん]局[きょく]
items.meaning_mnemonic: A <kanji>facility</kanji> that handles <kanji>mail</kanji> and refuses to handle anything else is a <vocabulary>post office</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 今日、郵便局に行きます。
example_sentences.english: I'm going to the post office today.
example_sentences.furigana: 今日[きょう]、郵[ゆう]便[びん]局[きょく]に行[い]きます。

example_sentences.japanese: 郵便局はどこですか。
example_sentences.furigana: 郵[ゆう]便[びん]局[きょく]はどこですか。

example_sentences.japanese: 郵便局で彼女を待ちます。
example_sentences.english: I'll wait for her at the post office.
example_sentences.furigana: 郵[ゆう]便[びん]局[きょく]で彼[かの]女[じょ]を待[ま]ちます。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 図（と）＋書（しょ）＋館（かん）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Pack a <kanji>building</kanji> with every <kanji>map</kanji> ever folded and everything a brush could <kanji>write</kanji>, and you have a <vocabulary>library</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 図書館はどこですか。
example_sentences.furigana: 図[と]書[しょ]館[かん]はどこですか。

example_sentences.japanese: 私は毎日図書館に行く。
example_sentences.english: I go to the library every day.
example_sentences.furigana: 私[わたし]は毎[まい]日[にち]図[と]書[しょ]館[かん]に行[い]く。

example_sentences.japanese: 友達と図書館で本を読む。
example_sentences.english: I read books at the library with a friend.
example_sentences.furigana: 友[とも]達[だち]と図[と]書[しょ]館[かん]で本[ほん]を読[よ]む。

items.meaning_mnemonic: The <kanji>station</kanji> kanji and the <vocabulary>station</vocabulary> word are the same character, so they mean the same thing.

example_sentences.japanese: 駅で友達を待ちます。

example_sentences.furigana: 駅[えき]で友[とも]達[だち]を待[ま]ちます。

example_sentences.japanese: 午後に駅へ行きます。
example_sentences.english: I go to the station in the afternoon.
example_sentences.furigana: 午[ご]後[ご]に駅[えき]へ行[い]きます。

example_sentences.japanese: 駅で弁当を買いました。

example_sentences.furigana: 駅[えき]で弁[べん]当[とう]を買[か]いました。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 空（くう）＋港（こう）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Swap the sea out of a <kanji>harbor</kanji> for a stretch of <kanji>empty</kanji> sky, and the boats that dock there become planes at an <vocabulary>airport</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 空港はどこですか。
example_sentences.furigana: 空[くう]港[こう]はどこですか。

example_sentences.japanese: 明日、空港に行きます。
example_sentences.english: I'm going to the airport tomorrow.
example_sentences.furigana: 明日[あした]、空[くう]港[こう]に行[い]きます。

example_sentences.japanese: 空港でお茶を飲みます。
example_sentences.english: I'll drink tea at the airport.
example_sentences.furigana: 空[くう]港[こう]でお茶[ちゃ]を飲[の]みます。

items.meaning_mnemonic: A single narrow room: a counter worn smooth by elbows, a bell that jingles when the door swings, shelves of goods each wearing a price tag. That is a <vocabulary>shop</vocabulary>.
items.reading_mnemonic: Every shelf in the place is a <reading>messy</reading> landslide of jars and tins, and prising one purchase out of that heap is what buying from a <vocabulary>shop</vocabulary>, a <reading>みせ</reading>, feels like.

example_sentences.japanese: この店は安いです。
example_sentences.furigana: この店[みせ]は安[やす]いです。

example_sentences.japanese: 私は店で本を買いました。
example_sentences.english: I bought a book at the shop.
example_sentences.furigana: 私[わたし]は店[みせ]で本[ほん]を買[か]いました。

example_sentences.japanese: 明日、友達とあの店に行きます。
example_sentences.english: Tomorrow I'm going to that shop with a friend.
example_sentences.furigana: 明日[あした]、友[とも]達[だち]とあの店[みせ]に行[い]きます。

items.reading_composition: Kana only — the word is written exactly as it is read.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Its floors are so many that you <reading>depart</reading> the basement for menswear like you are boarding a train. Any shop that vast is a <vocabulary>department store</vocabulary>, a <reading>デパート</reading>.

example_sentences.japanese: 私はデパートに行きます。
example_sentences.english: I'm going to the department store.
example_sentences.furigana: 私[わたし]はデパートに行[い]きます。

example_sentences.japanese: デパートで本を買いました。
example_sentences.english: I bought a book at the department store.
example_sentences.furigana: デパートで本[ほん]を買[か]いました。

example_sentences.japanese: このデパートは安いです。
example_sentences.furigana: このデパートは安[やす]いです。

items.reading_composition: Kana only — the word is written exactly as it is read.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The corner grocer kept adding aisles until a plain <reading>super</reading> in the name stopped sounding like a boast. A market big enough to earn that word is a <vocabulary>supermarket</vocabulary>, a <reading>スーパー</reading>.

example_sentences.japanese: 私はスーパーで魚を買います。
example_sentences.english: I buy fish at the supermarket.
example_sentences.furigana: 私[わたし]はスーパーで魚[さかな]を買[か]います。

example_sentences.japanese: 週末にスーパーへ行きませんか。
example_sentences.english: Shall we go to the supermarket this weekend?
example_sentences.furigana: 週[しゅう]末[まつ]にスーパーへ行[い]きませんか。

example_sentences.japanese: あのスーパーのお菓子はおいしい。
example_sentences.english: The snacks at that supermarket are delicious.
example_sentences.furigana: あのスーパーのお菓[か]子[し]はおいしい。

items.reading_composition: Kana only — the word is written exactly as it is read.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Koichi's shop sells socks, stamps and hot coffee at three in the morning without blinking. A store built entirely around being that <reading>convenient</reading> is a <vocabulary>convenience store</vocabulary>, a <reading>コンビニ</reading>.

example_sentences.japanese: コンビニでお茶を買います。
example_sentences.english: I buy tea at the convenience store.
example_sentences.furigana: コンビニでお茶[ちゃ]を買[か]います。

example_sentences.japanese: 明日コンビニに行きます。
example_sentences.english: I'm going to the convenience store tomorrow.
example_sentences.furigana: 明日[あした]コンビニに行[い]きます。

example_sentences.japanese: このコンビニは安いです。
example_sentences.furigana: このコンビニは安[やす]いです。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 公（こう）＋園（えん）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Take a patch of trees and mown grass, then make it <kanji>public</kanji> so any stranger can wander in and sit down. That open ground is a <vocabulary>park</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 私は毎日公園へ行く。
example_sentences.english: I go to the park every day.
example_sentences.furigana: 私[わたし]は毎[まい]日[にち]公[こう]園[えん]へ行[い]く。

example_sentences.japanese: 公園でお弁当を食べる。
example_sentences.english: I eat a boxed lunch at the park.
example_sentences.furigana: 公[こう]園[えん]でお弁[べん]当[とう]を食[た]べる。

example_sentences.japanese: あの公園は楽しいです。
example_sentences.english: That park over there is fun.
example_sentences.furigana: あの公[こう]園[えん]は楽[たの]しいです。

items.meaning_mnemonic: The <kanji>town</kanji> kanji and the <vocabulary>town</vocabulary> word are one and the same, so the meaning carries straight over.
items.reading_mnemonic: Sei strikes a <reading>match</reading> on the dark mountain trail, and the flame shows her she is standing in the main square of a whole <vocabulary>town</vocabulary> that was empty fields at dusk. She keeps the 「<reading>まち</reading>」 lit so it cannot slip back into the dark.

example_sentences.japanese: 週末に町へ行きます。
example_sentences.english: I'm going to town this weekend.
example_sentences.furigana: 週[しゅう]末[まつ]に町[まち]へ行[い]きます。

example_sentences.japanese: 町でパンを買いました。
example_sentences.furigana: 町[まち]でパンを買[か]いました。

example_sentences.japanese: この町の公園は楽しいです。
example_sentences.english: The park in this town is fun.
example_sentences.furigana: この町[まち]の公[こう]園[えん]は楽[たの]しいです。

items.mnemonic_text: The settlement grown past a town: shi.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The <kanji>city</kanji> kanji standing on its own is the whole word, so this <vocabulary>city</vocabulary> means exactly what the kanji does.

example_sentences.furigana: 週[しゅう]末[まつ]に友[とも]達[だち]と市[し]の公[こう]園[えん]で遊[あそ]びます。

example_sentences.furigana: 先[せん]月[げつ]、家[か]族[ぞく]とあの市[し]へ行[い]きました。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 映（えい）＋画（が）＋館（かん）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: The hall of moving pictures: eigakan.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Koichi rigs his konbini so the back wall <kanji>projects</kanji> a giant moving <kanji>picture</kanji>; once the whole <kanji>building</kanji> exists only to show that picture, he has opened a <vocabulary>cinema</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.english: This weekend I'm going to the cinema.
example_sentences.furigana: 週[しゅう]末[まつ]、映[えい]画[が]館[かん]に行[い]きます。

example_sentences.english: I watched a movie at the cinema.
example_sentences.furigana: 映[えい]画[が]館[かん]で映[えい]画[が]を見[み]ました。

example_sentences.japanese: この映画館は安いです。
example_sentences.furigana: この映[えい]画[が]館[かん]は安[やす]いです。

items.reading_composition: Irregular — へや cannot be assembled from the dictionary readings of 部屋.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Wall off one <kanji>section</kanji> of the <kanji>house</kanji>, hang a door on it, and that boxed-in piece is a <vocabulary>room</vocabulary>.
items.reading_mnemonic: Grandma Kane throws open a door at the shrine and barks 「<reading>へや</reading>」 at the cats hiding inside, which is just <reading>hey, you</reading> aimed at whoever will not come out of that <vocabulary>room</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.furigana: この部屋[へや]は寒[さむ]いです。

example_sentences.japanese: 部屋で本を読みます。
example_sentences.english: I read a book in the room.
example_sentences.furigana: 部屋[へや]で本[ほん]を読[よ]みます。

example_sentences.japanese: 友達の部屋に行きます。
example_sentences.english: I'm going to my friend's room.
example_sentences.furigana: 友[とも]達[だち]の部屋[へや]に行[い]きます。

items.reading_composition: Kana only — the word is written exactly as it is read.
items.meaning_mnemonic: An undignified raccoon at the riverbank keeps zapping the shallows with a <reading>toy ray</reading> gun, and every hit floats a porcelain <vocabulary>toilet</vocabulary> up out of the water and off downstream. By dusk the river is nothing but 「<reading>トイレ</reading>」 all the way to the bend.

example_sentences.japanese: トイレに行きます。
example_sentences.furigana: トイレに行[い]きます。

example_sentences.japanese: このトイレを使います。
example_sentences.furigana: このトイレを使[つか]います。

example_sentences.japanese: 駅のトイレはあそこです。
example_sentences.english: The station toilet is over there.
example_sentences.furigana: 駅[えき]のトイレはあそこです。

items.meaning_mnemonic: The room set aside for you to <kanji>wash</kanji> your <kanji>hand</kanji> in is the one polite people call the <vocabulary>restroom</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: お手洗いはあそこです。
example_sentences.furigana: お手[て]洗[あら]いはあそこです。

example_sentences.japanese: お手洗いに行きます。
example_sentences.furigana: お手[て]洗[あら]いに行[い]きます。

example_sentences.japanese: コンビニのお手洗いに入ります。
example_sentences.english: I'm going into the convenience store restroom.
example_sentences.furigana: コンビニのお手[て]洗[あら]いに入[はい]ります。

items.reading_composition: Mixed — 台（だい）on'yomi ＋ 所（どころ）kun'yomi.
items.meaning_mnemonic: A squat stone <kanji>stand</kanji>, the kind built to hold up a bronze statue, gets shoved into the one <kanji>place</kanji> you cook. That corner is now the <vocabulary>kitchen</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 私は台所に入ります。
example_sentences.furigana: 私[わたし]は台[だい]所[どころ]に入[はい]ります。

example_sentences.japanese: 台所でお茶を飲みます。
example_sentences.english: I drink tea in the kitchen.
example_sentences.furigana: 台[だい]所[どころ]でお茶[ちゃ]を飲[の]みます。

example_sentences.japanese: 台所の窓を開けます。

items.mnemonic_text: The green space by the house: niwa.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Picture the strip of bare ground that a Japanese house wraps itself around, half swept dirt and half stubborn weeds. The family still points at that patch and proudly calls it the <vocabulary>garden / yard</vocabulary>.
items.reading_mnemonic: Nao kneels on the strip of swept dirt the house wraps around, and each stubborn weed she yanks makes her yelp <reading>nee-wah</reading>, 「<reading>にわ</reading>」, in the family's proud <vocabulary form="庭">garden</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 子供は庭で遊びます。
example_sentences.english: The kids play in the yard.
example_sentences.furigana: 子[こ]供[ども]は庭[にわ]で遊[あそ]びます。

example_sentences.japanese: 父は今、庭に出ます。
example_sentences.english: Dad is heading out to the garden now.
example_sentences.furigana: 父[ちち]は今[いま]、庭[にわ]に出[で]ます。

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女は庭で本を読みます。
example_sentences.english: She reads a book in the garden.
example_sentences.furigana: 彼[かの]女[じょ]は庭[にわ]で本[ほん]を読[よ]みます。

items.meaning_mnemonic: The <kanji>road</kanji> kanji and the <vocabulary>road / street</vocabulary> word are the exact same character, so they mean the exact same thing.
items.reading_mnemonic: <reading>Mitch</reading> cranes his long neck to stare down the <vocabulary form="道">road</vocabulary> before his feet will advance a single step, and only then mutters 「<reading>みち</reading>」 and walks it.

example_sentences.japanese: この道を行きます。
example_sentences.furigana: この道[みち]を行[い]きます。

example_sentences.japanese: 道はどこですか。
example_sentences.furigana: 道[みち]はどこですか。

example_sentences.japanese: 友達と道で会います。
example_sentences.english: I'll meet my friend on the street.
example_sentences.furigana: 友[とも]達[だち]と道[みち]で会[あ]います。

items.meaning_mnemonic: The left riverbank and the right riverbank are tired of shouting across the water, so a long plank gets laid from one to the other. You walk over on that plank, and it is a <vocabulary>bridge</vocabulary>.
items.reading_mnemonic: A ferryman on the riverbank keeps warning that the current is <reading>harsh</reading>, so the villagers stop listening and build <reading>はし</reading> to cross on dry feet. That word now means the <vocabulary>bridge</vocabulary> that ended his job.

example_sentences.japanese: あの橋は高いです。
example_sentences.english: That bridge over there is tall.
example_sentences.furigana: あの橋[はし]は高[たか]いです。

example_sentences.japanese: 橋で友達を待ちます。
example_sentences.english: I'll wait for my friend at the bridge.
example_sentences.furigana: 橋[はし]で友[とも]達[だち]を待[ま]ちます。

example_sentences.japanese: 今日、公園の橋に行きます。
example_sentences.english: Today I'm going to the bridge in the park.
example_sentences.furigana: 今日[きょう]、公[こう]園[えん]の橋[はし]に行[い]きます。

items.meaning_mnemonic: Every <vocabulary>corner</vocabulary> in the house is the spot where two walls give up going straight and slam into each other at a hard right angle.
items.reading_mnemonic: Movers swing an old <reading>car door</reading> through the house and jam it where two walls slam together at a hard right angle, and it sticks with a 「<reading>かど</reading>」 in that <vocabulary form="角">corner</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.furigana: 駅[えき]の角[かど]で友[とも]達[だち]を待[ま]ちます。

example_sentences.japanese: 角の店でパンを買います。

example_sentences.furigana: 角[かど]の店[みせ]でパンを買[か]います。

example_sentences.japanese: 公園の角に行きます。

example_sentences.furigana: 公[こう]園[えん]の角[かど]に行[い]きます。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 交（こう）＋番（ばん）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.meaning_mnemonic: A <vocabulary>police box</vocabulary> is one street-corner spot where police and the public <kanji>mingle</kanji> all day long. Officers keep it staffed by each taking a <kanji>turn</kanji> on duty there.

example_sentences.furigana: 交[こう]番[ばん]はどこですか。

example_sentences.japanese: 昨日、交番に行きました。

example_sentences.furigana: 昨日[きのう]、交[こう]番[ばん]に行[い]きました。

example_sentences.japanese: 交番で道を聞きました。

example_sentences.furigana: 交[こう]番[ばん]で道[みち]を聞[き]きました。

items.reading_composition: Kana only — the word is written exactly as it is read.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The <vocabulary>taxi</vocabulary> at the head of the rank is always the <reading>tacky</reading> one, fur on the dash and dice on the mirror. You wave down the tackiest car you can see and call out <reading>タクシー</reading>.

example_sentences.english: We wait for a taxi at the station.
example_sentences.furigana: 私[わたし]たちは駅[えき]でタクシーを待[ま]つ。

example_sentences.japanese: あのタクシーは安い。
example_sentences.english: That taxi over there is cheap.
example_sentences.furigana: あのタクシーは安[やす]い。

items.reading_composition: Kana only — the word is written exactly as it is read.
items.meaning_mnemonic: A city <vocabulary>bus</vocabulary> pulls in so heavy that the <reading>bass</reading> of its engine rattles the shelter glass. You feel that <reading>バス</reading> in your teeth before it even rounds the corner.

example_sentences.japanese: 駅でバスを待ちます。

example_sentences.furigana: 駅[えき]でバスを待[ま]ちます。

example_sentences.furigana: 明日[あした]バスで海[うみ]へ行[い]きます。

example_sentences.japanese: このバスはデパートへ行きます。

example_sentences.furigana: このバスはデパートへ行[い]きます。

items.mnemonic_text: The tree's origin, a book: hon.

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 新（しん）＋聞（ぶん）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.meaning_mnemonic: A <vocabulary>newspaper</vocabulary> gathers everything <kanji>new</kanji> that people around town managed to <kanji>hear</kanji>. By morning the whole pile is printed on your doorstep.

example_sentences.furigana: この携[けい]帯[たい]は安[やす]いです。

items.meaning_mnemonic: The picture on that glowing box in the corner is always <reading>terrible</reading>, yet the whole family stares at it for hours. That hypnotic screen of bad shows is the <vocabulary>TV</vocabulary>, the box everyone calls the <reading>テレビ</reading>.

items.reading_composition: Kana only — the word is written exactly as it is read.
items.meaning_mnemonic: A hiker stuffs a sack with straw and drops it flat on the mountain trail. He sprawls across that lumpy <reading>bed</reading> and sleeps like a log, and 「<reading>ベッド</reading>」 is what he mutters for his <vocabulary>bed</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 私はベッドで寝ます。
example_sentences.furigana: 私[わたし]はベッドで寝[ね]ます。

example_sentences.japanese: このベッドは高いです。
example_sentences.furigana: このベッドは高[たか]いです。

example_sentences.japanese: 彼はベッドで本を読む。
example_sentences.furigana: 彼[かれ]はベッドで本[ほん]を読[よ]む。

items.reading_composition: Kana only — the word is written exactly as it is read.
items.meaning_mnemonic: A ghost keeps drifting straight through the wall until the landlord bolts a hinged slab across the gap. Now the ghost has to shove that <reading>door</reading> like everyone else, so the slab it resents is the <vocabulary>door</vocabulary> it hisses 「<reading>ドア</reading>」 at.

example_sentences.japanese: ドアを開けます。
example_sentences.furigana: ドアを開[あ]けます。

example_sentences.japanese: そのドアを閉めます。
example_sentences.furigana: そのドアを閉[し]めます。

example_sentences.japanese: 部屋のドアから入ります。
example_sentences.english: I go in through the room's door.
example_sentences.furigana: 部屋[へや]のドアから入[はい]ります。

items.meaning_mnemonic: Punch a square hole in a solid wall and fill it with a sheet of glass. Now you can watch the storm without a single drop landing on you, and that glass-filled square you stare through is a <vocabulary>window</vocabulary>.
items.reading_mnemonic: A <reading>mad doe</reading> out in the storm stares at you through the glass-filled square in the wall, rain streaming down her face but never yours, and you name that <vocabulary form="窓">window</vocabulary> 「<reading>まど</reading>」.

example_sentences.japanese: どの窓を開けますか。
example_sentences.furigana: どの窓[まど]を開[あ]けますか。

example_sentences.japanese: 私は窓から海を見ます。
example_sentences.english: I look at the sea from the window.
example_sentences.furigana: 私[わたし]は窓[まど]から海[うみ]を見[み]ます。

example_sentences.japanese: 寒いので、窓を閉めます。
example_sentences.english: It's cold, so I'm closing the window.
example_sentences.furigana: 寒[さむ]いので、窓[まど]を閉[し]めます。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 電（でん）＋気（き）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The <kanji>electricity</kanji> trapped in your walls picks up the restless <kanji>spirit</kanji> of a whole field, and the bulb overhead blazes awake. Flip the switch and that surge is <vocabulary>electricity / light</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 家の電気は高いです。
example_sentences.english: The electricity at home is expensive.
example_sentences.furigana: 家[いえ]の電[でん]気[き]は高[たか]いです。

example_sentences.japanese: 夜は部屋で電気を使います。
example_sentences.english: At night I use the lights in my room.
example_sentences.furigana: 夜[よる]は部屋[へや]で電[でん]気[き]を使[つか]います。

example_sentences.japanese: その電気はどこですか。
example_sentences.furigana: その電[でん]気[き]はどこですか。

items.meaning_mnemonic: Every locked door has just one small metal shape that will turn it, and that shape is a <vocabulary>key / lock</vocabulary>.
items.reading_mnemonic: The landlord turns <reading>cagey</reading> when you ask which small metal shape will turn your locked door, mutters 「<reading>かぎ</reading>」 and pockets the only <vocabulary form="鍵">key</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: この鍵でドアを開けます。
example_sentences.english: I open the door with this key.
example_sentences.furigana: この鍵[かぎ]でドアを開[あ]けます。

example_sentences.japanese: 鍵はかばんにあります。
example_sentences.english: The key is in the bag.
example_sentences.furigana: 鍵[かぎ]はかばんにあります。

example_sentences.japanese: 家の鍵を買いました。
example_sentences.furigana: 家[いえ]の鍵[かぎ]を買[か]いました。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 写（しゃ）＋真（しん）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: A copy of the truth: shashin.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Freeze one moment as a <kanji>true</kanji> copy, exact enough that nobody can deny it happened. That undeniable copy of real life is a <vocabulary>photograph</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: これは私の家族の写真です。
example_sentences.english: This is a photo of my family.
example_sentences.furigana: これは私[わたし]の家[か]族[ぞく]の写[しゃ]真[しん]です。

example_sentences.japanese: 昨日、友達の写真を見ました。
example_sentences.english: Yesterday I looked at my friend's photos.
example_sentences.furigana: 昨日[きのう]、友[とも]達[だち]の写[しゃ]真[しん]を見[み]ました。

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女の写真はどこですか。
example_sentences.furigana: 彼[かの]女[じょ]の写[しゃ]真[しん]はどこですか。

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 手（て）＋紙（がみ）. Rendaku: 紙 かみ → がみ.
items.meaning_mnemonic: You fill a sheet of <kanji>paper</kanji> with words in your own <kanji>hand</kanji>, then fold it up and mail it. What lands in the far mailbox is a <vocabulary>letter</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 昨日彼女に手紙を書いた。
example_sentences.english: I wrote her a letter yesterday.
example_sentences.furigana: 昨日[きのう]彼[かの]女[じょ]に手[て]紙[がみ]を書[か]いた。

example_sentences.japanese: 毎日父の手紙を読む。
example_sentences.english: I read Dad's letters every day.
example_sentences.furigana: 毎[まい]日[にち]父[ちち]の手[て]紙[がみ]を読[よ]む。

example_sentences.japanese: この手紙は難しい。
example_sentences.furigana: この手[て]紙[がみ]は難[むずか]しい。

items.reading_composition: Irregular — きって cannot be assembled from the dictionary readings of 切手.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Stamps come joined in a big sheet, so you <kanji>cut</kanji> one free by <kanji>hand</kanji> along the row of little holes. That torn-off square you lick and stick is a <vocabulary>postage stamp</vocabulary>.
items.reading_mnemonic: Kiki the tree spirit licks the back of a tiny <reading>kitty</reading> sticker and smooths it onto a letter. She giggles 「<reading>きって</reading>」, because to her that lickable little square is a <vocabulary>postage stamp</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 郵便局で切手を買います。
example_sentences.english: I'll buy stamps at the post office.
example_sentences.furigana: 郵[ゆう]便[びん]局[きょく]で切[きっ]手[て]を買[か]います。

example_sentences.japanese: この切手はいくらですか。
example_sentences.furigana: この切[きっ]手[て]はいくらですか。

example_sentences.japanese: 明日、切手を買いに行きます。
example_sentences.english: Tomorrow I'm going to buy stamps.
example_sentences.furigana: 明日[あした]、切[きっ]手[て]を買[か]いに行[い]きます。

items.meaning_mnemonic: Anything with six stiff flat sides and a lid you must lift before you can see what is inside is a <vocabulary>box</vocabulary>.
items.reading_mnemonic: A hawk stalks round all six stiff sides of a shut <vocabulary form="箱">box</vocabulary>, screeching <reading>hah-koh</reading>, 「<reading>はこ</reading>」, until someone lifts the lid to show it what is inside.

example_sentences.japanese: この箱を開けてください。
example_sentences.furigana: この箱[はこ]を開[あ]けてください。

example_sentences.japanese: 私は店で箱を買いました。
example_sentences.english: I bought a box at the shop.
example_sentences.furigana: 私[わたし]は店[みせ]で箱[はこ]を買[か]いました。

example_sentences.japanese: 箱に本があります。
example_sentences.english: There's a book in the box.
example_sentences.furigana: 箱[はこ]に本[ほん]があります。

items.reading_composition: Kana only — the word is written exactly as it is read.
items.meaning_mnemonic: You scribble one <reading>note</reading>, then a hundred more, then clamp the whole pile flat between two cardboard covers. That fat brick of paper is a 「<reading>ノート</reading>」, your <vocabulary>notebook</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 私はノートを買います。
example_sentences.furigana: 私[わたし]はノートを買[か]います。

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女はノートに書きます。
example_sentences.furigana: 彼[かの]女[じょ]はノートに書[か]きます。

example_sentences.japanese: このノートは安いです。
example_sentences.furigana: このノートは安[やす]いです。

items.meaning_mnemonic: A coat is fabric that has agreed to <kanji>obey</kanji> your body. It bends when your elbow bends, never argues, and a closet full of that obedient cloth is your <vocabulary>clothes</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: この服は高いです。
example_sentences.furigana: この服[ふく]は高[たか]いです。

example_sentences.japanese: デパートで服を買います。
example_sentences.english: I'm buying clothes at the department store.
example_sentences.furigana: デパートで服[ふく]を買[か]います。

example_sentences.japanese: 明日、友達と服を見ます。
example_sentences.english: Tomorrow I'll look at clothes with a friend.
example_sentences.furigana: 明日[あした]、友[とも]達[だち]と服[ふく]を見[み]ます。

items.meaning_mnemonic: The two leather cages you lock your feet into every morning, so you can stomp across gravel without a second thought, are your <vocabulary>shoes</vocabulary>.
items.reading_mnemonic: A barefoot hiker crosses the riverbank stones and picks up sharp <reading>cuts</reading> on both soles. She pulls on 「<reading>くつ</reading>」 so the next crossing scratches the <vocabulary>shoes</vocabulary>, not her feet.

example_sentences.japanese: この靴は高いです。
example_sentences.furigana: この靴[くつ]は高[たか]いです。

example_sentences.japanese: デパートで靴を買いました。
example_sentences.english: I bought shoes at the department store.
example_sentences.furigana: デパートで靴[くつ]を買[か]いました。

example_sentences.japanese: 靴はどこですか。
example_sentences.furigana: 靴[くつ]はどこですか。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 帽（ぼう）＋子（し）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Take a piece of full-size <kanji>headgear</kanji> and shrink it down to <kanji>child</kanji> size. What perches on one head now, light and small, is a <vocabulary>hat</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: この帽子は安いです。
example_sentences.furigana: この帽[ぼう]子[し]は安[やす]いです。

example_sentences.japanese: 店で帽子を買いました。
example_sentences.english: I bought a hat at the shop.
example_sentences.furigana: 店[みせ]で帽[ぼう]子[し]を買[か]いました。

example_sentences.japanese: 帽子はどこですか。
example_sentences.furigana: 帽[ぼう]子[し]はどこですか。

items.reading_composition: Kana only — the word is written exactly as it is read.
items.meaning_mnemonic: You button the cloth from collar to hem until it <reading>shuts</reading> flat against your chest. That sealed panel of fabric you tuck into your trousers is a <vocabulary>shirt</vocabulary>, the one you call 「<reading>シャツ</reading>」.

example_sentences.japanese: このシャツは高いです。
example_sentences.furigana: このシャツは高[たか]いです。

example_sentences.japanese: 明日シャツを買います。
example_sentences.furigana: 明日[あした]シャツを買[か]います。

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女のシャツはどこですか。
example_sentences.furigana: 彼[かの]女[じょ]のシャツはどこですか。

items.reading_composition: Kana only — the word is written exactly as it is read.
items.meaning_mnemonic: On a tennis <reading>court</reading> frozen solid in January, both players keep rallying in a full <vocabulary>coat</vocabulary> and thick gloves, because 「<reading>コート</reading>」 is too cold to play in anything less.

example_sentences.japanese: デパートでコートを買いました。
example_sentences.english: I bought a coat at the department store.
example_sentences.furigana: デパートでコートを買[か]いました。

example_sentences.japanese: このコートは高いです。
example_sentences.furigana: このコートは高[たか]いです。

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女のコートを見ます。
example_sentences.furigana: 彼[かの]女[じょ]のコートを見[み]ます。

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 天（てん）＋気（き）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.meaning_mnemonic: <kanji>Heaven</kanji> picks an <kanji>energy</kanji> level every morning. Whether it comes out sparking and stormy or flat and grey, that level is the <vocabulary>weather</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 今日の天気はいいです。
example_sentences.furigana: 今日[きょう]の天[てん]気[き]はいいです。

example_sentences.japanese: 明日はどんな天気ですか。
example_sentences.english: What kind of weather will it be tomorrow?
example_sentences.furigana: 明日[あした]はどんな天[てん]気[き]ですか。

example_sentences.japanese: 天気がいいから公園に行きます。
example_sentences.english: The weather's nice, so I'm going to the park.
example_sentences.furigana: 天[てん]気[き]がいいから公[こう]園[えん]に行[い]きます。

items.mnemonic_text: Drops from the sky frame: ame.
items.meaning_mnemonic: You have met this shape already: the <kanji>rain</kanji> kanji and the <vocabulary>rain</vocabulary> word are the very same character, so the meaning does not shift at all.
items.reading_mnemonic: <reading>Amy</reading> presses her nose to the window under the flat roof and counts the four dashes falling down each side of the glass, calling every one 「<reading>あめ</reading>」, the <vocabulary form="雨">rain</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 今日は雨です。
example_sentences.furigana: 今日[きょう]は雨[あめ]です。

example_sentences.japanese: 雨で傘を買います。
example_sentences.english: I'll buy an umbrella because of the rain.
example_sentences.furigana: 雨[あめ]で傘[かさ]を買[か]います。

example_sentences.japanese: 夕方から雨が来ます。
example_sentences.english: It'll start raining in the evening.
example_sentences.furigana: 夕[ゆう]方[がた]から雨[あめ]が来[き]ます。

items.meaning_mnemonic: Rain that dawdled on the way down until it froze arrives as soft white clumps on your collar. That heaped, silent pile is <vocabulary>snow</vocabulary>.
items.reading_mnemonic: A soft white clump slides off your collar and down your back, and the cold melt makes you groan 「<reading>ゆき</reading>」, because <vocabulary form="雪">snow</vocabulary> down the neck is <reading>yucky</reading>.

example_sentences.japanese: 今日は雪です。
example_sentences.furigana: 今日[きょう]は雪[ゆき]です。

example_sentences.japanese: 窓から雪を見る。
example_sentences.english: I watch the snow from the window.
example_sentences.furigana: 窓[まど]から雪[ゆき]を見[み]る。

example_sentences.japanese: 子供が雪で遊ぶ。
example_sentences.english: The kids are playing in the snow.
example_sentences.furigana: 子[こ]供[ども]が雪[ゆき]で遊[あそ]ぶ。

items.meaning_mnemonic: This character is an old friend by now: the <kanji>wind</kanji> kanji and the <vocabulary>wind</vocabulary> word are one and the same, so nothing about the meaning changes.
items.reading_mnemonic: One slash of air lifts a beetle off the picnic table along with the strip of <reading>gauze</reading> it sat on, and the gauze snaps out flat: 「<reading>かぜ</reading>」, real <vocabulary form="風">wind</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 今日は風が寒いです。
example_sentences.furigana: 今日[きょう]は風[かぜ]が寒[さむ]いです。

example_sentences.japanese: 窓から風が入る。
example_sentences.english: Wind comes in through the window.
example_sentences.furigana: 窓[まど]から風[かぜ]が入[はい]る。

example_sentences.japanese: 海の風がいいです。
example_sentences.furigana: 海[うみ]の風[かぜ]がいいです。

items.meaning_mnemonic: Koichi leaves a bag of cotton balls open by the till, the ceiling fan catches them, and a grey clump ends up hovering over the onigiri shelf where nobody can reach it. That floating, unreachable fluff is a <vocabulary>cloud</vocabulary>.
items.reading_mnemonic: A pigeon perched on Koichi's onigiri shelf coos 「<reading>くも</reading>」, <reading>coo-moh</reading>, at the grey cotton fluff the ceiling fan keeps spinning just out of reach, its own little <vocabulary form="雲">cloud</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 窓から雲を見ます。
example_sentences.english: I look at the clouds from the window.
example_sentences.furigana: 窓[まど]から雲[くも]を見[み]ます。

example_sentences.japanese: 今日は雲がありません。
example_sentences.furigana: 今日[きょう]は雲[くも]がありません。

example_sentences.japanese: 雲が一つ出ました。
example_sentences.furigana: 雲[くも]が一[ひと]つ出[で]ました。

items.meaning_mnemonic: The <kanji>sky</kanji> kanji, the one you also met as 'empty', and the <vocabulary>sky</vocabulary> word are a single character doing both jobs, so one wide empty space overhead is all either of them means.
items.reading_mnemonic: The digging crew punches clean through the roof of the empty hollow in the hill, looks up at the endless blue <vocabulary form="空">sky</vocabulary>, and cheers 「<reading>そら</reading>」, <reading>so, rah</reading>!

example_sentences.japanese: 今日の空はいい。
example_sentences.furigana: 今日[きょう]の空[そら]はいい。

example_sentences.japanese: 窓から空を見る。
example_sentences.english: I look at the sky from the window.
example_sentences.furigana: 窓[まど]から空[そら]を見[み]る。

example_sentences.japanese: 空から雨が来る。
example_sentences.furigana: 空[そら]から雨[あめ]が来[く]る。

items.meaning_mnemonic: The <kanji>sun / day</kanji> kanji is the whole of the <vocabulary>sun / day</vocabulary> word, one character with no extra pieces bolted on, so its meaning never shifts.
items.reading_mnemonic: When dawn climbs behind the tall window with one bar, its first ray hits Hiro square in the eyes. He hisses <reading>hee</reading>, <reading>ひ</reading>, glaring at the <vocabulary form="日">sun</vocabulary> through the glass.

example_sentences.japanese: 朝、日が出る。
example_sentences.english: In the morning, the sun comes out.
example_sentences.furigana: 朝[あさ]、日[ひ]が出[で]る。

example_sentences.japanese: 窓から日が入る。
example_sentences.english: The sun comes in through the window.
example_sentences.furigana: 窓[まど]から日[ひ]が入[はい]る。

example_sentences.japanese: 今日はいい日です。
example_sentences.furigana: 今日[きょう]はいい日[ひ]です。

items.meaning_mnemonic: You already carry this character as the <kanji>moon</kanji> kanji, and the <vocabulary>moon</vocabulary> word asks nothing more of it: same shape, same meaning.
items.reading_mnemonic: At night Suki the skier presses her goggles to the tall window with two bars and sighs <reading>ski</reading>, <reading>つき</reading>, because the pale <vocabulary form="月">moon</vocabulary> behind the glass has lit up the slope.

example_sentences.japanese: 夜、月を見ます。
example_sentences.english: At night, I look at the moon.
example_sentences.furigana: 夜[よる]、月[つき]を見[み]ます。

example_sentences.japanese: 空に月があります。
example_sentences.english: There's a moon in the sky.
example_sentences.furigana: 空[そら]に月[つき]があります。

example_sentences.japanese: 公園で月を見ます。
example_sentences.english: I look at the moon in the park.
example_sentences.furigana: 公[こう]園[えん]で月[つき]を見[み]ます。

items.meaning_mnemonic: Every night the sky quietly sets out thousands of tiny lamps and never sends anyone the bill. Each cold pinprick of light hanging up there is a <vocabulary>star</vocabulary>.
items.reading_mnemonic: Each night a lamplighter climbs up to light the sky's thousands of tiny lamps. Asked if the sky ever sends a bill, he chuckles <reading>ho, she</reading> never does, <reading>ほし</reading>, and lights one more <vocabulary form="星">star</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 窓から星を見ます。
example_sentences.english: I look at the stars from the window.
example_sentences.furigana: 窓[まど]から星[ほし]を見[み]ます。

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女は星の本を読みます。
example_sentences.english: She reads a book about stars.
example_sentences.furigana: 彼[かの]女[じょ]は星[ほし]の本[ほん]を読[よ]みます。

example_sentences.japanese: 明日の夜、星を見に行きます。
example_sentences.english: Tomorrow night I'll go see the stars.
example_sentences.furigana: 明日[あした]の夜[よる]、星[ほし]を見[み]に行[い]きます。

items.meaning_mnemonic: The one thing wide enough that you cannot see the far side, deep enough that nothing you drop comes back, and salty enough to sting a cut is the <vocabulary>sea</vocabulary>.
items.reading_mnemonic: A sailor steps off the last dock, sees nothing but water clear to the horizon, thumps his chest and booms 「<reading>うみ</reading>」, like <reading>ooh, me</reading>. All that flat endless salt water in front of him is the <vocabulary>sea</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 明日、海に行きます。
example_sentences.english: Tomorrow I'm going to the sea.
example_sentences.furigana: 明日[あした]、海[うみ]に行[い]きます。

example_sentences.japanese: 海で魚を見ました。
example_sentences.english: I saw a fish at the sea.
example_sentences.furigana: 海[うみ]で魚[さかな]を見[み]ました。

example_sentences.japanese: 私たちは海で遊びます。
example_sentences.furigana: 私[わたし]たちは海[うみ]で遊[あそ]びます。

items.meaning_mnemonic: The <kanji>mountain</kanji> kanji and the <vocabulary>mountain</vocabulary> word are the same character start to finish, so you already know everything it means.
items.reading_mnemonic: A stubborn <reading>llama</reading> trots across the flat ground to the three peaks, then plants its feet and brays <reading>やま</reading> at the tall middle one, the top of the <vocabulary form="山">mountain</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 私は山に行きます。

items.meaning_mnemonic: Those three flowing strokes are the <kanji>river</kanji> kanji, and the <vocabulary>river</vocabulary> word is that same character unchanged: one drawing, one meaning.
items.reading_mnemonic: A soggy dog hauls itself out where three streams flow side by side, then <reading>cower</reading>s on the bank whimpering <reading>かわ</reading> at the fast water the three make together, the <vocabulary form="川">river</vocabulary>.

items.meaning_mnemonic: The <kanji>tree</kanji> kanji, trunk and branches and roots in the dirt, is exactly the <vocabulary>tree</vocabulary> word, the same character standing for the same thing.
items.reading_mnemonic: Kiki, the tree spirit, slides down the trunk, swings on the one flat branch and tickles the two slanted roots, giggling <reading>key</reading>, <reading>き</reading>, all over her <vocabulary form="木">tree</vocabulary>.

items.meaning_mnemonic: The <kanji>flower</kanji> kanji and the <vocabulary>flower</vocabulary> word are one and the same character, so the bloom it draws is the bloom it means.
items.reading_mnemonic: A hen named <reading>Hannah</reading> pecks through the green grass until one blade changes its top into bright colour, then clucks <reading>はな</reading> and guards that new <vocabulary form="花">flower</vocabulary>.

items.meaning_mnemonic: The animal that hears your car three streets away and is losing its mind at the door before your key is out is a <vocabulary>dog</vocabulary>.
items.reading_mnemonic: Your car is heard three streets away, and by the time your key is out the thing behind the door yelps <reading>a new</reading> arrival, <reading>いぬ</reading>, again and again. That furry doorbell is your <vocabulary form="犬">dog</vocabulary>.

items.meaning_mnemonic: It shoves a glass off the table, watches it drop, holds your eye the whole time, then strolls away. That animal is a <vocabulary>cat</vocabulary>.

items.meaning_mnemonic: Anything that can sit on a branch, let go, and still not fall is a <vocabulary>bird</vocabulary>.
items.reading_mnemonic: A squirrel copies what it saw on the branch, lets go, and drops, its tail <reading>tore</reading> on the twigs. Above it, the one that let go and never fell chirps <reading>とり</reading>: a <vocabulary form="鳥">bird</vocabulary>.

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 動（どう）＋物（ぶつ）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.meaning_mnemonic: On the farm the nameless <kanji>thing</kanji> in the yard gets written off as junk. The one that <kanji>moves</kanji> itself to a warm corner with nobody pushing it is an <vocabulary>animal</vocabulary>.

items.meaning_mnemonic: You give up on a bare brown branch as dead wood. A week later it is covered in green buds, and that overnight comeback is <vocabulary>spring</vocabulary>.
items.reading_mnemonic: Gardener <reading>Harold</reading> nearly saws off the bare brown branch as dead wood, then spots green buds on it a week later and gasps <reading>はる</reading>: the branch is back, and so is <vocabulary form="春">spring</vocabulary>.

items.meaning_mnemonic: By breakfast your shirt is stuck to your back and the ice in your glass is gone in a minute. When the sun is still glaring at eight at night, it is <vocabulary>summer</vocabulary>.
items.reading_mnemonic: At eight at night the sun is still glaring, and a cloud of <reading>gnats</reading> sticks to your sweaty shirt and drowns in your melted ice. You swat and mutter <reading>なつ</reading>, because that is <vocabulary form="夏">summer</vocabulary>.

items.meaning_mnemonic: The leaves let their green drain out, go the colour of dry straw, and drop. Crops come in, the evenings turn sharp, and that long wind-down is <vocabulary>autumn</vocabulary>.
items.reading_mnemonic: A caretaker at the school rakes a mat of fallen leaves off the running track, every one the same dull <reading>khaki</reading>, and grunts 「<reading>あき</reading>」. The season that strips the trees and browns the field is <vocabulary>autumn</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 今年の秋は寒いです。
example_sentences.furigana: 今年[ことし]の秋[あき]は寒[さむ]いです。

example_sentences.furigana: 秋[あき]に友[とも]達[だち]と公[こう]園[えん]で遊[あそ]びます。

items.meaning_mnemonic: Your breath shows indoors and the puddles wear a lid of ice by morning. The days shrink to a short grey window, and that hard still stretch is <vocabulary>winter</vocabulary>.
items.reading_mnemonic: Leaving work, a commuter finds only a <reading>few</reading> minutes of grey light left in the sky and grumbles 「<reading>ふゆ</reading>」 at the dark. The season that keeps trimming every day down to nothing is <vocabulary>winter</vocabulary>.

items.meaning_mnemonic: A puddle you step over and a river is gone before you look twice. Water that just lies there in one huge still sheet you could row across for an hour is a <vocabulary>lake</vocabulary>.
items.reading_mnemonic: A boy on the lakeshore is sure the flat water is a quiet old woman named <reading>Miz Oomi</reading>, and every morning he greets it with 「<reading>みずうみ</reading>」. The huge calm sheet he waves at is a <vocabulary>lake</vocabulary>.

example_sentences.japanese: 夏に友達と湖で遊びます。

items.meaning_mnemonic: Take it all out and the world is a grey photocopy. The red of a stop sign or the green of a leaf, dropped back in, is <vocabulary>color</vocabulary>.

items.meaning_mnemonic: The <kanji>white</kanji> kanji and the <vocabulary>white</vocabulary> word are the very same character, so the meaning carries straight across with nothing added.

items.mnemonic_text: Divide it and grasp it: wakaru.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The <kanji>understand</kanji> kanji and the <vocabulary>to understand</vocabulary> word are the same character, so the meaning carries straight over. The kana tacked on the end makes it a verb that just happens on its own.

items.meaning_mnemonic: Once a fact is stuck to you firmly enough that you can produce it the second someone asks, it is yours. Carrying it around like that, always within reach, is what it means to <vocabulary>know</vocabulary> it.

items.meaning_mnemonic: Your two hands are the first pockets anyone ever had. Close your fingers around a thing and carry it off, and you <vocabulary>have</vocabulary> it.
